html:
SMTO-RST-0008 — SMTO doesn't recognize that cleanup choice

GUID: 58607f02-92e6-462c-9096-bcb690b5ab97
Slug: retention-action-invalid
Domain: RST · Subsystem: rst

What happened

  • The request asked SMTO to delete a kind of conversation data it doesn't offer, so nothing was deleted.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Reload the page so it matches the SMTO server you're using. A page left open across an SMTO update can send a cleanup choice the server doesn't accept.
  2. Open the conversation's Retention menu and choose one of its listed options, such as Delete summaries or Delete conversation history. Only the options in that menu are cleanup choices SMTO supports.

What success looks like

  • SMTO shows Retention action completed for the conversation.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't keep sending the same cleanup request; it will be refused the same way each time.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The conversation retention purge received an action outside its supported set (ui_chat, conversation, summaries, artifacts, receipts, diagnostics, everything).

What this means

  • Retention purge receives an action outside its advertised ACTIONS set. State diagnostics preserve authoritative journal, ownership and effect evidence. They do not delete records, loosen ownership fences, issue SQL or restart/replay work; missing persistence confirmation is separate from in-memory acceptance.

Why this can happen

  • Retention purge receives an action outside its advertised ACTIONS set.

How to diagnose it

  • Compare the requested action with current supported conversation/artifact retention controls.

How to fix it

  • native.retention.purge rejected an action not in ACTIONS. Fix the caller of DELETE /api/agent/native-conversations/<conversation_id>?action=... so it sends one of ui_chat, conversation, summaries, artifacts, receipts, diagnostics or everything; do not resubmit the same invalid value.
  • Choose a retention action advertised for the current conversation or artifact.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • An intentional supported retention action passes ordinary ownership and active-work checks.

What not to do

  • Do not repeatedly submit the same invalid input; correct the named constraint first.

Technical notes

  • State diagnostics preserve authoritative journal, ownership and effect evidence. They do not delete records, loosen ownership fences, issue SQL or restart/replay work; missing persistence confirmation is separate from in-memory acceptance.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
